blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court itself must resolve the disputed number of votes needed to convict Vice President Sara Z. Duterte because the Constitution gives the Senate the sole power to try and decide impeachment cases, House impeachment team adviser and spokesperson Ace Barbers said Friday. Barbers said the competing interpretations presented by former Supreme Court magistrates reinforce the need for senator-judges to make their own determination on how the constitutional two-thirds requirement should apply. “The change in the threshold is now in the hands of the Senate,” Barbers said during an online press briefing.
